To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the in vivo synthesis of taurocholate was decreased in rats fed ethionine for a period of 34 days, but was not altered in rats subjected to bile duct obstruction.
the conjugation of cholate in liver is impaired by ethionine, but not by 3′-me-DAB or 22-af, or by bile duct ligation.

the conjugation of cholate with taurine in the livers from rats fed ethionine is decreased to less than 1% of normal values, that the decrease is not seen in the livers after feeding of 3′-me-dab or 2-aa-f, and that bile duct ligation does not affect conjugation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of carcinogens and other hepatotoxic agents on the synthesis and metabolism of bile acids in the liver.
the metabolic changes that accompany hepatocarcinogenesis and the possible role of these changes in carcinogenesis.
the metabolism of bile components during experimental liver carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a defect in conjugation of cholate with taurine occurs during liver cancer induction by ethionine but not by 3′-me-DAB or 1-AAF.

the conjugation of cholate with taurine in vitro is not impaired in the livers during the development of liver tumors in rats fed 3'-Me-DAB or ethionine, but that the conjugation is impaired in rats subjected to bile duct obstruction.

the defect in taurochenodeoxycholic acid synthesis in ethionine-induced hepatocarcinogenesis is not due to a primary effect of the carcinogen, 3′Me-DAB, or 2-AAFA, nor to a secondary effect of bile duct ligation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
conjugation of choline is not impaired in the livers from rats with experimental hepatocarcinogenesis induced by ethionine or by 3′-M-DAB or 3-AAF.
the defect in taurochenodeoxycholic acid synthesis in ethionine-induced hepato-carcinogenesis is not due to a defect in the conjugation of cholate with taurine.
a defect in taurochenodeoxycholate synthesis is found in the litters of rats fed ethionine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the defect in tauroconjugation in the livers is specific for ethionine and does not occur with other hepatocarcinogens.
the defect in conjugation of bile salts is not a universal feature of hepatocarcinogenesis.
the liver microsomes are the major site of conjugation of bile components, and the conjugation of taurocholic acid is impaired in livers of rats with hepatocellular carcinoma.
